common.readOnlyNotice: your account is read-only. ask an admin to make changes.

language.title: language
language.hint: Saved in this browser. Missing your language, or found a wrong word? Help translate pingtxt on <link>Crowdin</link>.

login.firstRun: First run: create the admin account for this instance.
login.recoveryHint: lost your phone? type one of your recovery codes instead.

dashboard.title: monitors
dashboard.emptyState: no monitors yet. <link>create the first one</link>

monitor.deleteText: All results and incidents of this monitor will be deleted.
monitor.inMaintenance: in maintenance: <hl>{name}</hl> until {until}. checks keep running, alerts and incidents are paused.

http.label: http(s)
http.hint: request a URL and check the status code

keyword.label: keyword
keyword.hint: request a URL and look for a string in the body

tcp.label: tcp port
tcp.hint: open a TCP connection. IPv6 in brackets: [2001:db8::1]:443

ping.label: ping (icmp)
ping.hint: send ICMP echo requests (ICMPv6 for IPv6 addresses)

dns.label: dns
dns.hint: resolve a record and optionally match the answer

docker.label: docker container
docker.hint: down when the container is not running or unhealthy

mcp.label: mcp server
mcp.hint: initialize handshake and tools/list on a remote MCP server

smtp.label: smtp
smtp.hint: read the greeting, EHLO and STARTTLS when offered

push.label: heartbeat (push)
push.hint: your cron job or service calls a URL; down when the calls stop

monitorForm.name: name
monitorForm.pushHint: pingtxt gives this monitor a secret URL. Call it at the end of every run of your job: the monitor goes down when no call arrives within the expected period plus the grace time. The URL is shown after saving.
monitorForm.dockerHint: Checked on the docker engine of each selected location: the hub or agent needs access to /var/run/docker.sock (or DOCKER_HOST). With docker, mount it with -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock:ro.
monitorForm.grpcHint: grpc:// for plaintext, grpcs:// for TLS. The path is the service name to check; leave it out to check the whole server.
monitorForm.mcpMinToolsHint: optional: down when tools/list returns fewer
monitorForm.mcpToolsHint: optional, comma-separated: down when one is missing
monitorForm.mcpHeadersHint: one per line, sent with every request. Hidden from read-only users
monitorForm.expectedValueHint: optional: first column of the first row must equal this
monitorForm.keywordHint: case-sensitive substring of the response body
monitorForm.invertHint: fail when the keyword is present
monitorForm.expectedAnswerHint: optional: fail if no answer contains this
monitorForm.groupHint: groups show as sections on the dashboard and status pages
monitorForm.tagsHint: type a name and press enter to create a tag
monitorForm.graceHint: extra wait before the monitor goes down, e.g. for slow runs
monitorForm.retriesHint: consecutive failures before a location is down
monitorForm.locationsHint: The monitor is down when more than half of the online locations fail, degraded when at least the threshold below fails.
monitorForm.expiryHint: Notify before the TLS certificate or the domain registration expires. Thresholds are set in settings.

ipFamily.label: ip version
ipFamily.hint: IPv4 or IPv6 only, to catch one of them broken on a dual-stack host

responseRules.title: response checks
responseRules.hint: Rules on the JSON body. All must pass, otherwise the check fails and the alert says which rule broke. Paths look like checks.redis.status or items[0].id.

pushInfo.title: push url
pushInfo.cronComment: crontab: ping only when the job succeeds
pushInfo.failureComment: report the outcome either way, with the run time in ms
pushInfo.hint: Call this URL (any method) at the end of every run. Optional parameters: status=down to report a failed run, msg= for a short note, ping= for the run time in ms. Keep it secret: anyone with the URL can send heartbeats.
pushInfo.confirmText: The current URL stops working immediately. Update your jobs with the new one.

badges.title: badges
badges.hint: SVG images for a README, served without login through the status page "{page}". They refresh every minute and show only what the page already shows.
badges.pageHint: SVG image with the overall state of this page, for a README. It refreshes every minute.
badges.needsPage: Badges need a published status page that shows this monitor. Add it to one in <link>status pages</link>.

latencyChart.failed: {count, plural, one {# failed check} other {# failed checks}}

phaseChart.noData: no phase data yet: HTTP checks from the hub and updated agents measure it

uptimeBars.degradedChecks: {count, plural, one {# check} other {# checks}} while degraded
uptimeBars.maintChecks: + {count, plural, one {# check} other {# checks}} in maintenance

maintenance.title: maintenance
maintenance.intro: During a maintenance window checks keep running but the covered monitors show as maintenance: no incidents are opened and no alerts are sent, and those checks don't count toward uptime. If a monitor is still down when the window ends, the alert fires then.
maintenance.dialogText: Alerts are paused for the selected monitors while the window is active.
maintenance.name: name
maintenance.monthDaysHint: Months without that day are skipped.
maintenance.labelsHint: Groups and tags also cover monitors added to them later.

groups.title: groups & tags
groups.intro: A monitor belongs to at most one group and can have any number of tags. Groups are sections on the dashboard and on status pages; both can be used to pick monitors for maintenance windows and to filter the monitor list.
groups.noTags: no tags yet. you can also create them from the monitor form.
groups.deleteGroupText: Its monitors are kept, without a group. The group is removed from maintenance windows and status pages.
groups.deleteTagText: The tag is removed from every monitor and maintenance window.
groups.groupDialogText: Pick the monitors in this group. A monitor moved here leaves its previous group.
groups.name: name
groups.tagDialogText: Tags are free labels, like the environment or the team.

agents.title: agents
agents.intro: Agents are tiny probes you run anywhere (VPS, home lab, another cloud region) to check your monitors from more than one place. The hub itself is always available as the built-in location.
agents.devBuild: development build: agents are not updated
agents.updateHint: agents installed with the script update to this version when they connect. Docker agents update with the image.
agents.empty: no agents yet. add one to monitor from a second location.
agents.rotateText: The current token stops working immediately and the agent disconnects. You will get new install commands.
agents.deleteText: The agent is disconnected and removed from all monitors. Past results are kept.
agents.dialogText: The location label is what you see on charts, e.g. "Frankfurt".
agents.name: name
agents.installText: Run one of these on the machine that should become a monitoring location.

agentInstall.hint: The agent only dials out to the hub over HTTPS/WebSocket: no ports to open. The token is shown only now; rotate it to get a new one.

notifications.title: notifications
notifications.intro: Every enabled channel receives a message when a monitor goes down and when it recovers. A channel can also wait before alerting, to escalate long outages to another contact, and repeat the alert while the monitor stays down.
notifications.empty: no channels. you won't be alerted when something breaks.
notifications.dialogText: Use "send test" to check the configuration before saving.
notifications.name: name
notifications.delayHint: Minutes down before the first alert. 0 = right away. With a delay the channel only hears about outages still going on by then: use it for an escalation contact.
notifications.repeatHint: 0 = once. Otherwise a reminder is sent while the monitor stays down (at least {min}).

reports.title: periodic reports
reports.intro: An email with the uptime and the incidents of the last week or month, per monitor group, sent through your email channels.

kinds.weekly: weekly report, every Monday for the week before
kinds.monthly: monthly report, on the 1st for the month before

reports.channelsHint: Each selected channel sends the report to its recipients. Disabled channels are skipped.
reports.noEmail: No email channel yet: add one above to receive the reports.
reports.groupsHint: Pick groups to report only on them.
reports.hourHint: Hour of the day (0-23) the reports are sent.
reports.sent: report sent to {count, plural, one {# channel} other {# channels}}
reports.sentPartly: report sent to {count, plural, one {# channel} other {# channels}}, some failed: {error}
reports.previewHint: The preview uses the saved settings.

statusPages.title: status pages
statusPages.intro: Public pages that show the state and uptime history of the monitors you pick. Visitors see names and status only, never targets or error messages.
statusPages.deleteText: The public page stops working right away.

statusPageForm.descriptionPlaceholder: Live status of our public services.
statusPageForm.domainHint: Point a DNS record (CNAME or A) for this host at pingtxt and route it through the same reverse proxy, with its own TLS certificate. On that domain only this page is served, at /.
statusPageForm.publishedHint: drafts are visible only when you are logged in
statusPageForm.showIncidentsHint: start time and duration, without error details
statusPageForm.groupsHint: A group adds all its monitors, also the ones added later. Each group is a section with its name; monitors picked one by one come first, in their own order.
statusPageForm.onlyGroups: only the groups above. add single monitors from the list below.
statusPageForm.pickMonitors: pick monitors from the list below.
statusPageForm.allAdded: every monitor is on this page.
statusPageForm.subscribeHint: Visitors can subscribe by email to the incidents you post. Emails go out through the SMTP server and sender of this email channel, not to its recipients.
statusPageForm.subscribeNoChannel: Add an email channel in notifications to let visitors subscribe.

statusPublic.draft: draft: only you can see this
statusPublic.noIncidents: no incidents in the last {days} days.

subscribe.title: get updates
subscribe.sent: Check {email}: open the link we sent to confirm.
subscribe.hint: Incident updates by email. Every email has a link to unsubscribe.
subscribe.confirmed: {email} is subscribed: you will get incident updates by email.
subscribe.unsubscribed: {email} is unsubscribed: you will get no more emails.
subscribe.badLink: this link is not valid anymore.

settings.title: settings
settings.passwordChanged: password changed. other sessions were logged out.
settings.viewerHint: your account is read-only: you can see everything but cannot change monitors or settings. ask an admin if you need more.
settings.disconnectText: You will no longer be able to log in with this account.

generalSettings.publicUrlHint: used for agent install commands and login callbacks. empty: detected from the request (<hl>{url}</hl>).
generalSettings.localNameHint: name of the probe that runs inside the hub
generalSettings.localEnabledHint: off: checks run only from agents
generalSettings.retentionHint: hourly summaries for uptime, charts and status pages
generalSettings.rawRetentionHint: single results, at least 2 days. older ones live on in the hourly history
generalSettings.certDaysHint: one alert as each threshold is crossed, plus one when it expires. empty: off
generalSettings.domainDaysHint: looked up with rdap, or whois where rdap is missing (e.g. .it)
generalSettings.metricsPublicHint: off: scrapers need an api token (read scope is enough). on: anyone who can reach the hub can read monitor names and statuses
generalSettings.updateCheckHint: asks GitHub for the latest release every 12 hours and tells admins when one is out. off: the hub never contacts GitHub
generalSettings.missingScheme: no http:// or https:// in front: pick one
generalSettings.degradedPctHint: degraded when at least this share of a monitor's online locations fails, down when more than half do. monitors can override it

authSettings.title: authentication

help.github: create an OAuth app at <link>github.com/settings/developers</link> and use this callback url.
help.google: in <link>Google Cloud → Credentials</link> create an OAuth client ID of type "web application" and add this redirect URI.
help.oidc: any OpenID Connect provider: Authentik, Keycloak, Authelia, Pocket ID, Zitadel, Okta, Entra ID... register a client with this redirect URI.

authSettings.passwordLoginHint: turn off to allow only single sign-on. recovery: pingtxt -enable-password-login
authSettings.signup: create accounts on first single sign-on
authSettings.signupHint: off: only people who already have an account (same email) can log in with a provider
authSettings.domainsHint: comma separated, e.g. example.com. empty: any verified email
authSettings.secretSaved: saved. leave empty to keep it.
authSettings.needProvider: enable a provider before turning off password login

twoFactor.recoveryHint: save these recovery codes somewhere safe. each one works once, if you lose your phone. they are shown only now.
twoFactor.scan: scan the code with an authenticator app (1Password, Bitwarden, Aegis, Google Authenticator...), then type the 6 digit code it shows.
twoFactor.offHint: off · ask for a code from your phone after the password
twoFactor.codesLeft: {count, plural, one {# recovery code} other {# recovery codes}} left
twoFactor.manageHint: needed to turn it off or to get new recovery codes

apiTokens.intro: tokens let scripts and tools use the API. they cannot change accounts or settings.
apiTokens.copyNow: copy the token now, it will not be shown again.
apiTokens.name: name
apiTokens.viewerHint: your account is read-only: tokens can only read
apiTokens.revokeText: Scripts using this token stop working right away.
apiTokens.mcpIntro: AI assistants (Claude, Cursor…) connect to the MCP server at {url} by signing in with OAuth, or with a token.
apiTokens.mcpClaudeCode: connect Claude Code to the MCP server:
apiTokens.connectedApps: connected apps (signed in with OAuth to the MCP server)
apiTokens.disconnectText: The assistant loses access right away and has to sign in again.
apiTokens.apiDocs: API reference: <docs>interactive docs</docs> and the <spec>OpenAPI document</spec>.

viewer.label: read-only
viewer.hint: sees everything but secrets, changes nothing

users.reset2faText: Use this when they lost their phone and recovery codes. They are logged out and can set it up again.
users.deleteText: The user is logged out and can no longer log in.
users.viewerHint: read-only users see monitors, incidents and history but cannot change anything; passwords and tokens in monitors and notification channels are hidden from them.
users.passwordHint: empty: log in with single sign-on (same email)

backups.exportIntro: monitors, groups, tags, notification channels, maintenance windows, status pages, agents and instance settings as a JSON file. no history and no user accounts: use a database backup for that.
backups.withSecretsHint: the file will hold passwords, bot tokens, secret webhook urls, login client secrets and agent tokens. keep it safe.
backups.withoutSecretsHint: passwords, tokens and secret webhook urls are replaced by [redacted]. importing here keeps the stored values; on another hub those channels are skipped and those monitors paused until you fill them in.
backups.mergeHint: objects with the same name are updated, the others are added. nothing is deleted.
backups.replaceHint: deletes every monitor (with its history), group, tag, channel, maintenance window and status page first.
backups.applySettings: also apply instance settings (public url, login, retention...)
backups.noAutoBackup: no automatic backup with this database: back up the database server first if you may want to undo the import.
backups.autoBackup: a database backup is taken before importing.
backups.replaceText: Every current monitor, with its history, and every group, tag, channel, maintenance window and status page will be deleted, then the file is imported.
backups.restartToRestore: restart the hub to finish the restore
backups.dbIntro: a backup is a full copy of the database: settings, users, secrets and history. it is taken while the hub keeps running.
backups.pending: restore pending: <hl>{name}</hl> replaces the database when the hub restarts. the current database is kept as a pre-restore backup.
backups.restoreText: The database will be replaced by {name} when the hub restarts. Everything after {date} is lost; the current database is kept as a pre-restore backup.
backups.serverIntro: this hub stores its data in {db}. back up the database server with its own tools (or your provider's snapshots): the dump holds settings, users, secrets and history. the configuration export above works too, without history and users. with the docker compose files from the docs:

apiDocs.title: api reference
apiDocs.intro: Every endpoint of the hub's REST API. Try it out uses your browser session; to test a token, paste it in Authorize. Account and instance settings accept the browser session only.
apiDocs.error: could not load the API document: {error}

hubOffline.hint: getting ready, this page goes on by itself
hubOffline.unreachable: the hub is not reachable yet, this page goes on by itself when it is back

pageIncidents.intro: Tell visitors what is going on: open an incident and post updates until it is resolved. They show on the public page.
pageIncidents.introSubscribers: Tell visitors what is going on: open an incident and post updates until it is resolved. They show on the public page and are emailed to subscribers.
pageIncidents.messagePlaceholder: We are looking into slow responses of the API.
pageIncidents.postedNotified: posted, {count, plural, one {# email} other {# emails}} on the way
pageIncidents.deleteText: The incident and all its updates disappear from the public page. Emails already sent stay sent.
pageIncidents.subscriptionsOff: Subscriptions are off: pick a working email channel in the page settings. Nobody gets emails until then.
